raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38167.

When a diffusion forward fails with a CUDA error other than OOM (a driver error, a device-side assert, a caching-allocator assert), the device or its allocator can no longer be trusted. The worker logged the error, called `empty_cache()` and kept serving. Every later request either ran on the broken device or failed, and `/health` still returned `{"status": "ok"}`, so no orchestrator would restart the server.

In #38167 the trigger is PyTorch's expandable-segments allocator (pytorch/pytorch#188008, on WSL2 with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`). That needs a PyTorch fix. This PR makes the server fail cleanly instead of staying up broken.

## Modifications

This builds on the fail-closed path from #46025 instead of adding a separate unhealthy flag.

- `gpu_worker.py`: classify forward errors that leave the device unusable (`torch.AcceleratorError`, `CUDA driver error:`, `CUDA error:`, `HIP error:`, caching-allocator asserts, also through `__cause__`/`__context__`; anything mentioning "out of memory" is excluded). On one, log the restart guidance and raise `_FatalDeviceError`, a `SystemExit` like `_FatalDistributedForward`, so it escapes request-level recovery and skips `empty_cache()`. `run_scheduler_process` catches both and calls `os._exit(1)`.
- The HTTP server's backend monitor from #46025 then fails pending requests, rejects new POSTs with 503 and turns `/health` 503. OOM keeps its current recover-and-continue behavior on a single GPU.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. Successful requests take the same path as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. Nothing changes on a successful request.

## Tests

Live server on an RTX A6000 (torch 2.14.1+cu130, `Efficient-Large-Model/Sana_600M_512px_diffusers`). A temporary hook, not part of this PR, writes out of bounds on the GPU before `forward_fn()` when the prompt contains a marker, raising a real `CUDA error: device-side assert triggered`.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Normal request | 200 (3.2 s) |
| `/health` before | 200 |
| Request that triggers the assert | 500 after 1.1 s |
| Request queued 0.3 s behind it | 500 after 0.8 s |
| `/health` after, polled from 1.3 s to 11.6 s | 503 `{"status":"unhealthy","error":"Scheduler worker exited; restart the server."}` |
| New request | 503 in 1 ms |
| Scheduler process | exited (`<defunct>` until reaped) |
| GPU memory | 13.5 GB used before, 0.27 GB after |

No `empty_cache()` call after the error. Not covered: multi-rank runs and the original expandable-segments failure from #38167, which can't be triggered on demand.

Unit: `multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_unrecoverable_device_error.py` (CPU) covers the classifier and the exit path.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -264,6 +264,10 @@ class _FatalDistributedForward(SystemExit):
     """Escape request-level recovery when ranks can no longer run in lockstep."""
 
 
+class _FatalDeviceError(SystemExit):
+    """Escape request-level recovery when the device can no longer be trusted."""
+
+
 class GPUWorker(GPUWorkerPostTrainingMixin):
     """
     A worker that executes the model on a single GPU.
@@ -811,6 +815,16 @@ def _execute_forward_common(
                 raise _FatalDistributedForward(
                     "Multi-rank forward ran out of memory; restart the server."
                 ) from e
+            if _is_unrecoverable_device_error(e):
+                # The device can no longer be trusted and even empty_cache() may
+                # fail; exit so the HTTP backend monitor fails pending requests.
+                measure_server_warmup = False
+                logger.error(
+                    UNRECOVERABLE_DEVICE_ERROR_MSG.format(error=f"{error_context}: {e}")
+                )
+                raise _FatalDeviceError(
+                    "Unrecoverable device error; restart the server."
+                ) from e
             if propagate_forward_errors and forward_failed:
                 if isinstance(e, StopIteration):
                     raise RuntimeError(
@@ -1734,6 +1748,47 @@ def _oom_exceptions():
     return (torch.OutOfMemoryError,)
 
 
+UNRECOVERABLE_DEVICE_ERROR_MSG = """
+Unrecoverable device error in {error}
+The device or its memory allocator is in an unknown state, so this worker
+exits and the server stops accepting requests. Restart it.
+  - "CUDA driver error" or "!handles_.at(i) INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED" with
+    PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True: a non-OOM driver failure
+    while mapping memory leaves the allocator inconsistent
+    (https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/188008). It is most common on
+    WSL2/Windows near the memory limit; lower the resolution or memory use, or
+    run without expandable_segments.
+"""
+
+# Non-OOM device errors after which the CUDA context or the caching allocator
+# cannot be trusted, matched in the message because C10_CUDA_DRIVER_CHECK and
+# allocator asserts surface as plain RuntimeErrors.
+_UNRECOVERABLE_DEVICE_ERROR_MARKERS = (
+    "CUDA driver error:",
+    "CUDA error:",
+    "HIP error:",
+    "CUDACachingAllocator.cpp",
+)
+
+
+# An OOM stays recoverable: the allocator releases what it mapped, and the
+# cache is emptied after the request.
+def _is_unrecoverable_device_error(error: BaseException) -> bool:
+    seen = set()
+    while error is not None and id(error) not in seen:
+        seen.add(id(error))
+        if isinstance(error, _oom_exceptions()):
+            return False
+        message = str(error)
+        if "out of memory" not in message and (
+            isinstance(error, torch.AcceleratorError)
+            or any(marker in message for marker in _UNRECOVERABLE_DEVICE_ERROR_MARKERS)
+        ):
+            return True
+        error = error.__cause__ or error.__context__
+    return False
+
+
 def run_scheduler_process(
     local_rank: int,
     rank: int,
@@ -1776,12 +1831,10 @@ def run_scheduler_process(
             }
         )
         scheduler.event_loop()
-    except _FatalDistributedForward:
-        logger.exception(
-            "Worker %d cannot safely continue after a multi-rank OOM", rank
-        )
-        # CUDA/NCCL teardown can wait forever on a peer's outstanding collective.
-        # Exit at the process boundary; the HTTP worker monitor rejects new work.
+    except (_FatalDistributedForward, _FatalDeviceError) as e:
+        logger.exception("Worker %d cannot safely continue: %s", rank, e)
+        # CUDA/NCCL teardown can hang on a peer's collective and a broken
+        # allocator can fail in cleanup; the HTTP worker monitor rejects new work.
         os._exit(1)
     except _oom_exceptions() as _e:
         logger.warning(OOM_MSG)

@@ -0,0 +1,170 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""A non-OOM device error (#38167) must exit the worker instead of serving on a
+broken device while /health still reports ok."""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, Mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers import gpu_worker as gpu_worker_module
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers import scheduler as scheduler_module
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.managers.gpu_worker import (
+    GPUWorker,
+    _is_unrecoverable_device_error,
+)
+
+# the two errors reported in #38167, verbatim
+_DRIVER_ERROR = "CUDA driver error: device not ready"
+_ALLOCATOR_ASSERT = (
+    '!handles_.at(i) INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at "/__w/pytorch/pytorch/c10/cuda/'
+    'CUDACachingAllocator.cpp":467, please report a bug to PyTorch.'
+)
+
+
+def _wrapped(message: str) -> Exception:
+    try:
+        try:
+            raise RuntimeError(message)
+        except RuntimeError as cause:
+            raise ValueError("stage failed") from cause
+    except ValueError as error:
+        return error
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "error",
+    [
+        RuntimeError(_DRIVER_ERROR),
+        RuntimeError(_ALLOCATOR_ASSERT),
+        RuntimeError("CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered"),
+        _wrapped(_DRIVER_ERROR),
+    ],
+)
+def test_device_breaking_errors_are_unrecoverable(error):
+    assert _is_unrecoverable_device_error(error)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "error",
+    [
+        torch.OutOfMemoryError("CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB"),
+        RuntimeError("CUDA error: out of memory"),
+        ValueError("height must be divisible by 16"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_oom_and_request_errors_stay_recoverable(error):
+    assert not _is_unrecoverable_device_error(error)
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def worker(monkeypatch):
+    device = SimpleNamespace(reset_peak_memory_stats=Mock(), empty_cache=Mock())
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gpu_worker_module.torch, "get_device_module", lambda: device)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        type(gpu_worker_module.current_platform), "is_cpu", lambda self: False
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        type(gpu_worker_module.current_platform), "is_mps", lambda self: False
+    )
+    worker = GPUWorker.__new__(GPUWorker)
+    worker.is_output_rank = True
+    worker.server_args = SimpleNamespace(
+        pipeline_config=SimpleNamespace(supports_auto_residency=False)
+    )
+    worker._realtime_sessions = SimpleNamespace(attach=lambda req: None)
+    worker._release_warmup_pool = lambda req: None
+    worker._record_output_peak_memory = Mock()
+    return worker, device
+
+
+def _forward_raising(worker, error, propagate_forward_errors=False):
+    req = SimpleNamespace(
+        request_id="req",
+        is_warmup=False,
+        extra={},
+        metrics=None,
+        trace_ctx=MagicMock(),
+        log=lambda **kwargs: None,
+    )
+
+    def forward():
+        raise error
+
+    return worker._execute_forward_common(
+        req,
+        forward_fn=forward,
+        log_reqs=[req],
+        return_req=False,
+        save_output_paths=lambda output_batch: None,
+        error_context="request req",
+        propagate_forward_errors=propagate_forward_errors,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("propagate", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("message", [_DRIVER_ERROR, _ALLOCATOR_ASSERT])
+def test_device_error_exits_the_worker(worker, message, propagate):
+    worker, device = worker
+
+    # must escape the scheduler's request-level `except Exception` handlers
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="restart the server") as exc_info:
+        _forward_raising(worker, RuntimeError(message), propagate)
+
+    assert message in str(exc_info.value.__cause__)
+    # empty_cache on a broken allocator can raise out of the error handler
+    device.empty_cache.assert_not_called()
+    worker._record_output_peak_memory.assert_not_called()
+
+
+class _Exited(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+def test_scheduler_process_exits_on_device_error(monkeypatch):
+    for name in (
+        "initialize_current_platform",
+        "kill_itself_when_parent_died",
+        "configure_logger",
+        "globally_suppress_loggers",
+        "_bind_worker_to_gpu_numa_node",
+        "set_cuda_arch",
+        "set_musa_arch",
+        "init_diffusion_tracing",
+    ):
+        monkeypatch.setattr(gpu_worker_module, name, lambda *args, **kwargs: None)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gpu_worker_module.PortArgs, "from_server_args", lambda server_args: None
+    )
+
+    class _BrokenDeviceScheduler:
+        def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+            pass
+
+        def event_loop(self):
+            raise gpu_worker_module._FatalDeviceError(
+                "Unrecoverable device error; restart the server."
+            )
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(scheduler_module, "Scheduler", _BrokenDeviceScheduler)
+
+    events = []
+
+    def exit_(code):
+        events.append(("exit", code))
+        # the real os._exit never returns; raising lets the test continue
+        raise _Exited(code)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(gpu_worker_module.os, "_exit", exit_)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        gpu_worker_module.gc, "collect", lambda: events.append(("cleanup",))
+    )
+
+    with pytest.raises(_Exited):
+        gpu_worker_module.run_scheduler_process(
+            local_rank=0, rank=0, server_args=SimpleNamespace(), pipe_writer=Mock()
+        )
+
+    # exits at the process boundary before cleanup can touch the broken device
+    assert events[0] == ("exit", 1)
